problem: Prior VLN work improves generalization via training-time data augmentation or pretraining, effectively memorizing augmented data, and ignores distribution shift between train and unseen test environments at inference.
motivation: Test-time decisions should be invariant to irrelevant object changes and viewpoint shifts, yet agents degrade in unseen houses. The paper proposes adapting the agent on each test sample with a self-supervised visual-consistency objective, borrowing test-time training ideas.
key_idea: Add a MoCo-style contrastive visual/action consistency module (for both imitation and soft-actor-critic RL) to existing VLN agents, trained jointly and then adapted at test time with an entropy-minimization objective over augmented views.
insight: Test-time adaptation gives the largest gains beyond the train-time contrastive variant: VLN-BERT val-unseen SR goes 59.86 -> 62.22 (NNC) -> 67.18 (full). Ablations show that removing either contrastive loss (CL_IL or CL_RL) drops VLN-BERT unseen SR by roughly 13-17%, and dropping the supervised loss hurts badly, so the consistency loss complements rather than replaces supervision. Caveat: the paper is loosely specified and the adaptation cost is significant (inference time about 2-3x).
method: Base agents: model-agnostic; CLIP-ViL (EnvDrop-style seq2seq LSTM with CLIP ViT features) and VLN-BERT (recurrent BERT, initialized from PREVALENT).

Augmentation pool: instance-level visual modifications (following EnvDrop) plus feature-level dropout, sampled per step to make positive views of panoramic observations; negatives are temporally different observations from the same path.
Consistent semantic observation: MoCo query/key encoders with momentum update theta_k <- m theta_k + (1-m) theta_q, with contrastive loss between raw and augmented views.

Consistent teacher forcing / soft actor critic: contrastive losses L_CL^IL and L_CL^RL encourage similar action distributions and returns across positive pairs; RL uses SAC with a momentum key critic.
Joint training: L = L_ML + lambda L_CL, where L_ML = L_RL + lambda L_IL; 20000 iterations, lambdas all 0.2.
Test-time adaptation: freeze theta_ML, update only the self-supervised theta_CL per test sample for 10 iterations by minimizing prediction entropy over augmented views, then infer.

setting.backbone: CLIP-ViL (seq2seq LSTM + CLIP ViT) and VLN-BERT (recurrent BERT), both fine-tuned with added contrastive modules
setting.training_data: R2R and RxR training splits; augmentations of observations; baselines' pretraining (PREVALENT init for VLN-BERT, CLIP features)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with ResNet or ViT features plus instruction

numbers.extra: test-time adaptation on each test sample; single run

numbers_note: Only val-seen/val-unseen reported; no test-server results. The Human row in the table is empty.
results: On R2R val-unseen, DAVIS lifts VLN-BERT from SR 59.86 / SPL 55.09 to SR 67.18 / SPL 60.51, and CLIP-ViL from SR 52.45 / SPL 46.76 to 54.04 / 49.14. On RxR val-unseen, VLN-BERT sDTW rises 35.21 -> 37.16 and nDTW 53.12 -> 54.52. Gains hold for both architectures, with test-time adaptation giving extra improvement over train-time contrastive learning.
limitations: Test-time adaptation adds notable inference cost (e.g., VLN-BERT unseen 85s -> 190s).
Evaluated only on English-pivoted indoor R2R/RxR with discrete nav-graph; no test-server or multi-domain/low-resource evaluation.
Method description is loose; the fixed θ_ML vs adapted θ_CL split and the improvement magnitudes rely on single runs.
